land.text: the south of the united monarchy: Judah and Benjamin, after 'ten of the tribes rebelled against Rehoboam' c. 930 BCE

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Israel' row (-1000..-701, Wikipedia 'Kingdom of Israel (united monarchy)') spans the united monarchy and the northern kingdom.

land.text: 'the fallen kingdom was annexed as a Babylonian province', Yehud, with Mizpah in Benjamin as its centre

successors.note: The Babylonian province of Yehud was Judah's successor; it passed to the Achaemenid Empire as 'Yehud Medinata' (Kingdom of Judah page). Cliopatria's Neo-Babylonian row starts in -600, so its shapes overlap Judah for -600..-587.

capitals.name: Jerusalem
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Jerusalem'; coordinates are the gazetteer's Jerusalem.

correction.text: Judah's core as the page draws its frontier: from the north-western shore of the Dead Sea past Jericho to Gezer, across the Shephelah to Beersheba in the north Negev; the -900 shape unchanged

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Judah shape begins in -900, but the page dates the kingdom from the secession c. 930 BCE ('Jeroboam's Revolt: c. 930 BCE'; Rehoboam c. 931-913). The -900 shape (3,684 km2) is the best available core for the thirty earlier years. No infobox area exists to compare.

3,684 km2 (34.85-35.63 E, 31.34-31.91 N), -900..-801. The page describes the frontier in general terms: 'The northern border of Judah extended east–west from the northwestern shore of the Dead Sea, passing near Jericho to the area of Gezer'; 'To the west, the border ran from Gezer across the Shephelah to Beersheba in the northern Negev'; 'In prosperous periods, Judah's influence expanded, stretching southward to Beersheba and beyond'. The shape stops just north of Beersheba. No infobox area; the Judah-Israel border at Ramah/Mizpah is described but undated.

4,303 km2 (34.61-35.63 E), -800..-751: the -900 shape grown 620 km2 to the west (two cells, 34.74-34.86 E, 31.35-31.48 N), toward the Philistine plain. The Kingdom of Judah page (re-read 2026-10-19) says Tel Beit Shemesh and Tel Lachish 'became under influence of Judah later during the 9th or 8th centurty BCE'; a 3 km circle at Tel Lachish meets the added cells, so the growth is the Lachish side (ledger gain at -800, confidence 2). The page does not mention Uzziah, and the Uzziah page names no place. No infobox area.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, held to 702 instead of 701

keyframe_review.note: 4,303 km2, -750..-701, unchanged from -800. Sennacherib's invasion of 701 devastated the countryside, claimed 46 cities, and gave 'the surrounding towns to Assyrian vassal rulers in Ekron, Gaza and Ashdod', so the shape holds only to -702. Years only.

correction.text: Judah after 701: the hills round Jerusalem without the towns given to the vassal rulers of Ekron, Gaza and Ashdod

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -701..-586, which Cliopatria lacks (its Judah row ends in -701 though the kingdom lasted to 586). Jerusalem was besieged but not taken in 701; the Shephelah towns went to Ekron, Gaza and Ashdod; Judah then paid tribute to Assyria under Manasseh (c. 687/686-643/642), to Egypt from 609 and to Babylon from 605 (Kingdom of Judah page). The shape is the -701 shape without the Shephelah; nothing on the pages dates a later change of frontier. The tributary relations (Assyria 734-609, Egypt 608-605, Babylon 605-586) are vassal_start/vassal_end pairs in the ledger.

ledger.note: c. 930: Judah splits from Israel. 'ten of the tribes rebelled against Rehoboam' and formed the northern Kingdom of Israel (infobox 'Jeroboam's Revolt: c. 930 BCE'; 'c. 931-913 BCE: Rehoboam'), leaving Rehoboam in Jerusalem.

region.text: the Judah-Israel frontier in Benjamin, from the Dead Sea past Jericho to Gezer, with Mizpah and Geba on Judah's side and Ramah on the border

ledger.note: c. 930: Israel and Judah at war. 'Israel and Judah warred throughout Rehoboam's 17-year reign'; Baasha later 'built a fortress at Ramah on the border, less than ten miles from Jerusalem' and Asa fortified Geba and Mizpah in Benjamin 'on his side of the border' (no years).

region.text: the Judah-Israel frontier in Benjamin, from the Dead Sea past Jericho to Gezer, with Mizpah and Geba on Judah's side and Ramah on the border

ledger.note: c. 911: end of the fighting, bridged to the end of Abijah's reign. The Abijah of Judah page (opened 2026-10-19): reign 'c. 913 – 911 BCE' (infobox; 915/914 to 912/911 as the page's working dates), a march north 'in the 18th year of King Jeroboam I', the 'Battle of Mount Zemaraim' and the capture of Jeshanah, Ephron and Bethel; it gives no end or terms of the war and says Abijah died 'shortly after his campaign'. The Kingdom of Judah page ties the war to Rehoboam's 17-year reign and has the Baasha-Asa frontier fortresses (Ramah, Geba, Mizpah) undated, so the end is a bridge, not a treaty.

region.text: the strip added to Judah's shape at -800 on the Philistine side, taking in Tel Lachish, which with Tel Beit Shemesh 'became under influence of Judah later during the 9th or 8th centurty (sic) BCE'

ledger.note: 800: Judah's western edge advances toward Lachish. Kingdom of Judah page (re-read 2026-10-19): 'Similar discussion exists around Tel Beit Shemesh and Tel Lachish, who according to some scholars belong to the Shephelah and became under influence of Judah later during the 9th or 8th centurty BCE'. The year is the page's century placed at -800 and the land is my reading: on the gazetteer the shape's 620 km2 growth is two cells (34.74-34.86 E, 31.35-31.48 N) and a 3 km circle at Tel Lachish (34.85 E, 31.56 N) meets them, while Tel Beit Shemesh (35.01 E, 31.75 N) is already inside the -900 shape. Counterpart set to nobody (was philistia): Cliopatria's Philistia shapes of -900, -800 and -750 contain none of the two cells, so philistia has no loss to mirror, and the page names no earlier owner; the page speaks of 'influence', not conquest. The Uzziah page (opened 2026-10-19) says only that he 'conquered the Philistines and the Arabians' (2 Chronicles 26), names no place and does not tie it to Lachish or the Shephelah.

734: Judah becomes an Assyrian tributary. 'Asqaluna, Judah, Edom, Moab and Ammon, and the Mu'na Arab tribe, all began paying tribute to Tiglath-Pileser', in the campaign the Tiglath-Pileser III page dates 734 (it gives no separate year for the tribute; reopened 2026-10-19). The Kingdom of Judah page has only a footnote on a Tiglath-pileser III text naming Ahaz ('dated 734–733'), says Judah 'was a vassal of Assyrian rulers: Sennacherib and his successors' (Manasseh) and that Hezekiah 'paid three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold to Assyria' (701). Judah is the vassal and neo-assyrian-empire the suzerain; mirrors neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/13 (-734), whose counterpart there is free text ('Judah, Edom, Moab and Ammon'): me-02 should put kingdom-of-judah in it (reviewer fix).

region.text: the towns around Jerusalem and Lachish that Sennacherib 'was able to give ... to Assyrian vassal rulers in Ekron, Gaza and Ashdod'

ledger.note: 701: Sennacherib's campaign strips Judah. 'Sennacherib claimed the siege and capture of many Judaean cities, but only the siege—not capture—of Jerusalem'; 'After he besieged Jerusalem, Sennacherib was able to give the surrounding towns to Assyrian vassal rulers in Ekron, Gaza and Ashdod.' The prism claims 46 cities destroyed. The page does not name the towns; the Shephelah (the page's western border region, with Lachish besieged) is the researcher's reading.

609 (bridged): the Assyrian overlordship ends with the empire. The Kingdom of Judah page does not date the end of Assyrian rule over Judah: it says the Neo-Assyrian Empire 'was beginning to disintegrate' around Josiah's accession (c. 641/640), that Necho and Ashur-uballit II failed to hold Harran in 609 ('The event also marked the disintegration of the Assyrian Empire') and puts 'the final fall of the Neo-Assyrian Empire' in 605 BCE; 609 follows neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/57 (-609, the empire's end), which names Judah in free text. Judah was not subject to Egypt until Necho returned in 608.

608: Judah becomes an Egyptian vassal. Necho II led an army to the Euphrates 'in the spring of 609 BCE' and Josiah was killed at Megiddo; 'On his return march to Egypt in 608 BCE' Necho 'deposed Jehoahaz ... and replaced him with his older brother, Jehoiakim', and 'imposed on Judah a levy of a hundred talents of silver'; 'Jehoiakim ruled originally as a vassal of the Egyptians by paying a heavy tribute'. The reviewer gave 609; the page dates the levy to the return march, 608. Judah is the vassal and twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt (me-03) the suzerain, which has no mirror yet (reviewer fix).

605: the Egyptian overlordship ends at Carchemish: 'when the Egyptians were defeated by the Babylonians at Carchemish in 605 BCE, Jehoiakim changed allegiances to pay tribute to Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon'.

605: Judah pays tribute to Babylon (the sentence quoted above); after the deportation of 597 Zedekiah 'was made a tributary of Babylon'. neo-babylonian-empire /ledger/5 starts the vassalage at -597 (its Nebuchadnezzar II page: Jerusalem taken, Judah stays a vassal kingdom); this ledger follows the Kingdom of Judah page's 605, so that dossier (me-02) should move its start to -605 or accept the eight-year difference (reviewer fix).

589: Nebuchadnezzar returns. Zedekiah 'revolted against' Babylon and allied with Egypt; 'In 589 BCE, Nebuchadnezzar II returned to Judah and again besieged Jerusalem.' The first siege fell on 16 March 597 (Jeconiah and about 10,000 Judeans deported); Judah had paid tribute to Babylon since 605, after the Egyptians lost at Carchemish.

586: the tribute ends with the fall of Jerusalem and the annexation of the land as the Babylonian province of Yehud (the loss below). The page gives 586 and 587; neo-babylonian-empire /ledger/6 has -587, one year apart.

586: Jerusalem captured. 'Babylonian campaigns against Judah culminated in the capture of Jerusalem in 586 BCE, the destruction of the city, and the end of the Judahite monarchy' (the infobox gives the siege as c. 587 BCE and Zedekiah's reign as c. 597-587).

region.text: the fallen kingdom, annexed as a Babylonian province

ledger.note: 586: Judah becomes a Babylonian province. 'the fallen kingdom was annexed as a Babylonian province', Yehud; Gedaliah was governor, 'supported by a Babylonian guard', and the centre moved to Mizpah in Benjamin 'not Jerusalem'.
586: the Kingdom of Judah ends. Nebuchadnezzar 'put an end to the independent Kingdom of Judah'; infobox 'Succeeded by: Yehud (Babylonian province)'; Zedekiah is the last ruler (c. 597-587).

wars.name: Israel-Judah wars of Rehoboam

zones.text: the Judah-Israel frontier in Benjamin, from the Dead Sea past Jericho to Gezer, with Mizpah and Geba on Judah's side and Ramah on the border

wars.outcome: No decisive result; the kingdoms stay separate; Egypt's Shishak took many Judean cities in Rehoboam's fifth year (Judah an Egyptian vassal, 10th century BCE).
wars.note: The page has the frontier fortresses of Baasha (Ramah) and Asa (Geba, Mizpah) and the alliance by marriage between Jehoshaphat and Ahab, all undated. Reviewer thin note: the Abijah of Judah page (reign c. 913-911, the battle of Mount Zemaraim, Jeshanah, Ephron and Bethel taken) gives no end of the war, so the war is run to the end of Abijah's reign, -911 (confidence 1 in the ledger).

wars.name: Sennacherib's campaign against Judah

zones.text: the towns around Jerusalem and Lachish that Sennacherib 'was able to give ... to Assyrian vassal rulers in Ekron, Gaza and Ashdod'

wars.outcome: Hezekiah's refusal of tribute drew Sennacherib's invasion in 701; Judean fortified towns were destroyed or captured, Jerusalem was besieged but not taken, Hezekiah paid tribute, and the surrounding towns went to Assyrian vassal rulers in Ekron, Gaza and Ashdod.
wars.note: The Bible gives 300 talents of silver and 30 of gold as the tribute; the siege article's infobox calls the result 'Inconclusive - Both sides claim victory'. The siege article dates neither Hezekiah's refusal of tribute nor the tribute; the Kingdom of Judah page has Hezekiah sole ruler 'c. 715 BCE' (and 727-698 elsewhere).

wars.name: Josiah at Megiddo
wars.outcome: Josiah tried to block Necho II's march to the Euphrates at Megiddo and was killed; On his return march in 608 Necho deposed Jehoahaz, installed Jehoiakim and levied a hundred talents of silver; Judah was an Egyptian vassal until 605 (vassal pair in the ledger).

wars.name: Babylonian conquest of Judah
wars.outcome: Jehoiakim switched to Babylon after Carchemish (605); Jerusalem fell on 16 March 597; Zedekiah revolted and was besieged from 589; the city fell in 586 and Judah became the province of Yehud.

certainty.note: The page gives the frontier only in general terms (the Dead Sea, Jericho, Gezer, the Shephelah, Beersheba); no treaty or survey line.

Re-read 2026-10-19 for the reviewer fixes: Assyrian, Egyptian (608) and Babylonian (605) tribute, the Tel Lachish / Tel Beit Shemesh sentence.

sources.title: Siege of Jerusalem (701 BC)
sources.note: Sennacherib's invasion, Hezekiah's tribute, towns given to the vassal rulers of Ekron, Gaza and Ashdod, Jerusalem not taken.

notes:
Page budget 1-2 pages: the Kingdom of Judah page (queried three times) and the Siege of Jerusalem (701 BC) page were opened. For the review repair three more pages were opened (outside the budget): Tiglath-Pileser III (the 734 tribute), Abijah of Judah and Uzziah (the reviewer's thin notes). No infobox area on any page, so the 3.7k-4.3k km2 shapes are unchecked.

Review repair (2026-10-19): added the vassal pairs the reviewer found missing: Assyria -734..-609 (Tiglath-Pileser III page; the end is a bridge at confidence 1), Egypt -608..-605 and Babylon -605..-586 (Kingdom of Judah page). Mirrors wanted: neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/13 and /57 should name kingdom-of-judah; twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt (me-03) should add vassal_start -608 / vassal_end -605 with counterpart kingdom-of-judah; neo-babylonian-empire /ledger/5 (-597) and /6 (-587) should become -605 and -586/-587 (the Judah page gives 605 for the tribute; 586 and 587 for the fall). I dated the Egyptian start 608, not the reviewer's 609, because the page puts the levy and Jehoiakim's installation on Necho's return march 'in 608 BCE' (the campaign itself is spring 609). The -800 gain now cites the page's Tel Lachish sentence (confidence 2) and its counterpart is nobody: Philistia's shapes contain none of the strip's cells, so philistia (me-04-a) has no loss to add. The Israel-Judah war now ends -911 (Abijah's death) instead of -913.

Cliopatria's Judah row is -900..-701 (3 shapes), but the kingdom lasted c. 930-586; the dossier begins at -930 and ends -586 with two new keyframes (-930..-901, -701..-586). The -701..-586 shape is the -701 shape minus the Shephelah (a name for the gazetteer: the lowland between the Judean hills and the coastal plain, c. 34.7-35.1 E, 31.3-31.9 N).

Open points: (1) The Judah-Israel border after Abijah (Baasha at Ramah, Asa at Geba and Mizpah) is undated on every page opened. (2) Egypt's earlier overlordship under Shishak (Rehoboam's fifth year, 10th century) is not a ledger pair: the page gives no year. (3) Edom's revolt under Jehoram and the alliance by marriage with Ahab (Athaliah) are undated. (4) The Kingdom of Judah page dates Hezekiah's sole rule 'c. 715' in one place and 727-698 in another; his refusal of tribute is undated, so the war entry covers 701 only. (5) Philistia's dossier (another batch) carries the 701 gain from Judah. (6) No ruler strip is given: the page lists only Rehoboam first and Zedekiah last. (7) Gazetteer names wanted: Shephelah (region), Tel Lachish and Tel Beit Shemesh (places).
